targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. Toward the left end of the wall, left of Stegosaurus; the start is from the top of a boulder at the base.
targets.name: Scaling Scales

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It starts left of Ding Dong and right of Brennansaurus.
targets.name: Shake, Rattle & Roll

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It is in the centre of the corridor, just left of Say Ahh, starting up a chimney on the left side of a flake.
targets.name: Solosaurus

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It is a hand crack just left of Blowing Blood.
targets.name: Staudersaurus

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It is on the far left of the corridor, left of Brontosaurus.
targets.name: Stegosaurus

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It shares its start with Graves Danger, then breaks left.
targets.name: T-Rex

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, take the good trail that starts at the edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock. Skirt the base of the north face from the east to reach the entrance of the hidden corridor between the two opposing walls; some scrambling is needed to get to the climbs. The south-side routes are along the left wall as you enter. It is the easy right-slanting crack on the far right of the south side.
targets.name: Wheelchair Ramp

targets.approach: Lime-Aid is a northwest-facing formation to the south of Table Top Rock, a little to the southwest of Shark Fin. One way in is a straight climb on foot from the west end of Pioneer Lane; or by following the trail past The Gardens up the steep rocky hillside of the Upper Hill and splitting off to the formation. The route is on the right side of the west face.
targets.name: Fresh Squeezed

targets.approach: Drive up Keller Peak Road to Campsite 2. A trail starts near the campsite entrance and skirts it on the right; do not walk through the campsite when it is occupied. Little Pleasures Rock sits behind the campsite. The route climbs a right-facing lieback flake to a chimney on the east face, just left of Life's Little Pleasures.
targets.name: Ick

targets.approach: Drive up Keller Peak Road to Campsite 2. A trail starts near the campsite entrance and skirts it on the right; do not walk through the campsite when it is occupied. Little Pleasures Rock sits behind the campsite. It starts on the east face just left of Ick.
targets.name: No Pleasure At All

targets.approach: Use the approach that Morning Wall and Jedi Spire share: keep to the streambed and continue beyond the Jedi Spire turnoff. Lonesome Dove Rock is a big formation to the right of the stream; the east face has a distinctive recess at its centre, and the route climbs it.
targets.name: Texas Ranger

targets.approach: From the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead, hike up to Long Lake, a good spot to camp. The buttress shows through and above the trees to the northeast. The route starts around the corner left of Magic Staircase, on a clean white face cut by a hand crack, right below that route's second-pitch corner.
targets.descent_text: The climbs on this buttress are gear-only and the descent is a walk-off.
targets.name: Devil's Snare

targets.approach: From the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead, hike up to Long Lake, a good spot to camp. The buttress shows through and above the trees to the northeast. Look for the prominent second-pitch corner about halfway up the face, to the left of the wall's highest section; the first pitch is blocky fourth class to easy fifth class up to its base.
targets.descent_text: Build a gear belay at the top of the second pitch and walk off.
targets.name: Magic Staircase

targets.approach: From the north near Coyote Crag, hike west past Camp Rock to a clear, much-used path heading south into the trees; at the split keep left and continue southeast until the northwest corner of Lost Orbit Rock comes into view. From the southern parking area, head north beside the west side of Parkinglot Rock, then northeast on a faint trail to the south end of the formation. The route is the chimney behind the big tan flake, with Stand Up Comedy on the flake's left.
targets.name: Worm Hole
targets.peak: Lost Orbit Rock - East Face Left (Angry Inch Wall)

targets.approach: Take forest road 2N13 east from Green Valley Lake. Low Maintenance Rock is the nearest formation visible beside the road on the left, and you park on the roadside. The route starts low on the left, beside Couple of Pitons Here on its right, and traverses diagonally right and up.
targets.name: Close Talker

targets.approach: Take forest road 2N13 east from Green Valley Lake. Low Maintenance Rock is the nearest formation visible beside the road on the left, and you park on the roadside. It climbs the prow just right of Hat Head, where two pitons are visible from the base.
targets.name: Puffy Shirt

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail that starts at the southern edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock; the north face is the wall of chimneys and offwidths on that side. It is a dirty chimney just left of Is it Dinnertime Yet?.
targets.descent_text: Getting down from this face means either a roundabout walk-off or a rappel from the anchors at the top of a neighbouring bolted route.
targets.name: Balding in Peru

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail that starts at the southern edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock; the north face is the wall of chimneys and offwidths on that side. It sits at the left-hand extreme of the north face, left of Balding in Peru, with a finger crack to a horizontal and a short bolted crux.
targets.descent_text: Getting down from this face means either a roundabout walk-off or a rappel from the anchors at the top of a neighbouring bolted route.
targets.name: Desperately Seeking Slopers

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail that starts at the southern edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock; the north face is the wall of chimneys and offwidths on that side. It starts up the left-leaning wide crack of the neighbouring Bloody Ankles line, then continues up a squeeze chimney where that route breaks right.
targets.descent_text: Getting down from this face means either a roundabout walk-off or a rappel from the anchors at the top of a neighbouring bolted route.
targets.name: Is it Dinnertime Yet?

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail that starts at the southern edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock; the north face is the wall of chimneys and offwidths on that side. It starts next to Buzz Off and a pine tree on their right, up a hand crack that becomes a squeeze chimney.
targets.descent_text: Getting down from this face means either a roundabout walk-off or a rappel from the anchors at the top of a neighbouring bolted route.
targets.name: Sabre Tooth

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail that starts at the southern edge of Campsite 2 up to Lower Dinosaur Rock; the north face is the wall of chimneys and offwidths on that side. The start is a short way along from Desperately Seeking Slopers, beside a protruding column of rock; jam and layback the left side of the block that leans on the face.
targets.descent_text: Getting down from this face means either a roundabout walk-off or a rappel from the anchors at the top of a neighbouring bolted route.
targets.name: Why am I Here?

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It is a hand crack on the far left side of the face.
targets.name: Battle of the Bulge

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It starts on the left side of the face, just right of Battle of the Bulge, over a small roof.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted anchor at the top.
targets.name: Better than Dip

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It is in the centre of the face just right of South Crack; reach a ledge by scrambling from the right or by climbing South Crack, then follow the thin crack.
targets.name: Exit Stage Left

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It lies just right of the Last of the Dinosaurs line, on a right-slanting hand crack.
targets.name: Sapling Crack

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It is in the centre of the face, just right of Tighten Your Britches, up a right-facing flake.
targets.name: South Crack

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It is on the far right side of the face and climbs to the prominent roof.
targets.name: The Neighbor's Roof

targets.approach: From Keller Peak Road, follow the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, skirt along its east side, then turn west to reach the foot of the south face. It is in the centre of the face just right of Sapling Crack, up the outside of a big right-facing flake.
targets.name: Tighten Your Britches

targets.approach: Park in one of the turnouts beside the road at Courtright Reservoir, just before Trapper Springs Campground, and walk to the granite slabs; there is no real trail. Skirt the base of the dome's south faces to the Lower Tier. The route is a left-leaning crack to slab, right of the black water streak that carries the bolted line to its left; gear low, bolts above.
targets.name: Afro Sheen

targets.approach: Park in one of the turnouts beside the road at Courtright Reservoir, just before Trapper Springs Campground, and walk to the granite slabs; there is no real trail. Skirt the base of the dome's south faces to the Lower Tier. It is on the left margin of the huge shield, with Organ Grinder on one side and the direct start of Republicans on Crack on the other, climbing past bolts to a flake and on up the face.
targets.name: The Stroll

targets.approach: Pull off opposite Kidd Creek, cross the road, and take the worn track up the creek bed until boulder-hopping to the left bank becomes possible. From there a steep slope reaches the broad gully that serves The Underworld, and this buttress sits immediately right of that gully. The route is the slab just left of Toetally Broken.
targets.name: Broken Toess

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is a short way left of Golden Oldies on Golden Oldies Wall.
targets.name: Above Suspicion

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. Find it at the middle recess of the Requiem Wall.
targets.name: Babalu

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is down and right of Black Track.
targets.descent_text: From the end of the pitch, rappel to the first-pitch anchor of the neighbouring Black Track route.
targets.name: Crazy Train

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. Look to the right of the slot dividing the Black Track half of the wall from the Pump Up the Jams half, next to The Art of the Steal.
targets.name: Ozzmosis

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The first pitch shares its start with Flower Power on the Requiem Wall.
targets.name: Right to Lean P1

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route starts in the gully left of Hex Route in Sector Zero.
targets.name: Sector Zero

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. Find it on the Reality Show Wall, to the right of The Contender.
targets.name: Survivor

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. Find it on the Pump Up the Jams wall, two lines left of the obvious splitter that gives the wall its name.
targets.descent_text: Lower from the anchor at the end of the pitch.
targets.name: The Art of the Steal

targets.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is just left of The Apprentice on the Reality Show Wall.
targets.name: Unknown
